messages:
lina-cs: Hi team, Tom from KiteMetrics just reported 403s for generation calls but only when they send batched requests (single-item calls succeed). He pasted logs, says this started after a key rotation yesterday.

tom_kite: Repro steps I used:
- curl single: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer KEY' -d '{"input":"hello"}' -> 200
- curl batch: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer KEY' -d '{"inputs":["hi","hey"]}' -> 403

maria-support: Can you paste the raw error from the 403 response body?

tom_kite: Here it is:
{
  "error": "forbidden",
  "message": "missing scope: inference.generate",
  "status": 403
}

lina-cs: Thanks. Single-item generation works but batch path is returning missing scope for generation — sounds like the token being used lacks the batch/generation permission flag (we recently split batch handling permission checks).

alex-ml: Quick hypothesis: older keys had a combined "generation" flag; after SSO rotation their new svc key may have been provisioned with only [embeddings, rerank] scopes. The batch endpoint enforces inference.generate explicitly. Can you run the token introspect CLI? e.g.:

provisioner-bot: @tom_kite running token-introspect for KEY...\nscopes: ["embeddings.rerank", "embeddings.create"]\nissued_by: sso-provisioner\ncreated_at: 2026-03-15T22:04:10Z

maria-support: That matches alex's guess — generation scope absent.

tom_kite: Huh, that's weird because the UI checked boxes for "Generation" when we created the key. We use SSO automation, maybe a bug during rotation.

lina-cs: Possible workaround for them while we fix this: use an org-level API key that has generation scope, or re-run the provisioning flow manually and ensure the "generation" box is ticked. But we should fix root cause so SSO rotation preserves generation perms.

sam-platform: Filing an escalation to provisioning infra. @alex-ml can you add a quick check in the rotation logic to copy over the inference.generate flag? Also want audit log of rotations for this tenant.

alex-ml: I'll add a guard in the provisioner; plausible bug: our SCIM mapping drops the "inference.generate" claim when roles are mapped to service key scopes if the csv includes extra commas. I can triage and propose a patch.

maria-support: In the meantime I've advised Tom to rotate the key via the org console (manual path) and confirm scopes. He said he'll try now.

tom_kite: Manual rotation fixed it. New token introspect shows:
provisioner-bot: running token-introspect for NEWKEY...\nscopes: ["inference.generate", "embeddings.create", "embeddings.rerank"]\n
Result: batch requests now succeed. :white_check_mark:

lina-cs: Great. Root cause: rotation path via SSO automation dropped generation scope. Action items:
- sam-platform: create a short-term alert if token-introspect for new keys lacks any scopes the previous key had (to catch regressions)
- alex-ml: patch provisioner mapping to preserve inference.generate on rotations (investigate CSV parsing edge case)
- maria-support: reach out to KiteMetrics, confirm they can rotate via UI and link them to docs for key scopes

sam-platform: I'll create the alert and add an onboarding checklist item for teams using SSO rotation.

alex-ml: I'll follow up with a PR and include a regression test for a multi-scope rotation case.

maria-support: Noted and emailing Tom with steps and root-cause summary.

tom_kite: Thanks all — appreciated the quick response. If you want, I can share the rotation audit logs privately.

lina-cs: Please do; dropping them in support ticket would help. Closing thread once PR and alert are in. :)
